<!-- Generated from api/v1alpha1/well_known.go by `make well-known-doc`. Do not edit. -->

This page lists every label, annotation and finalizer key Bloodraven reads or writes, and its node taint, with the objects that carry each one, who writes it, the grammar of its value, and how stable it is:

- **Public**: you may set or select on it, and it changes only with a release-noted break.
- **Operator-owned read-only**: the operator writes it; you may read it, but do not edit or remove it.
- **Internal (may change)**: operator bookkeeping. Do not read or edit it; its key and value can change in any release.

Every key is under `bloodraven.shipstream.io`: the prefix itself (`bloodraven.shipstream.io/<name>`), or a subdomain of it for a family whose name part is an id (`<kind>-hold.bloodraven.shipstream.io/<id>`, `<namespace>.db-readonly.bloodraven.shipstream.io/<group>`), so one prefix match finds every member. The `app.kubernetes.io/*` labels the operator also sets are the Kubernetes recommended labels and are not listed. A boolean label value is `true` or `false`.

A structured internal value is a JSON object with a `schemaVersion` member. A payload with a version the operator does not know proves nothing: the operator refuses it and reports it with a condition and a Warning Event (`MetadataVersionUnsupported`), as each key below says.

## Action annotations

A user (or kubectl bloodraven) sets these on the MysqlFailoverGroup to request a one-shot action. They share one value grammar, `<subject>(:<key>=<value>)*`: the subject is a site name or an operation id, a pair splits at its first `=`, and a value matches `^[A-Za-z0-9._/+-]+$`, so it never contains `:` or `=`. An instant inside a value uses the ISO 8601 basic UTC form, for example `20261104T100000Z`. A destructive action on a site-name subject carries `confirm=<metadata.name>:uid=<metadata.uid>`; an operation id the operator minted and never reuses needs neither. Two keys are outside the grammar: RevokeDeploymentLeasesAnnotation is presence-only (its value is ignored), and RotateKeyringAnnotation takes a bare site name, since a rotation destroys nothing. A value that does not parse, or fails its interlock, is never acted on: each key's consumer reports why (a Warning Event, or the status of the request) and, for most keys, removes the annotation so the request can be set again; the entries below say which. Never commit an action annotation to a GitOps repository: a sync re-applies it.

| Key | On | Writer | Value and meaning | Stability |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `bloodraven.shipstream.io/planned-failover` (annotation) | MysqlFailoverGroup | user (kubectl bloodraven promote); the operator removes it | `<site>[:maxLagWait=<duration>]`, for example `pdx` or `pdx:maxLagWait=30s`; maxLagWait is 1s to 1h. This key triggers a graceful, cooldown-respecting switchover to the named PrimaryCandidate site. The operator removes it once the request is decided: accepted, rejected or skipped. A request that is deferred (onCooldown=Defer, a deployment hold), or that waits for admission, keeps it until then; removing it cancels a deferred run. | Public |
| `bloodraven.shipstream.io/acknowledge-planned-failover-hold` (annotation) | MysqlFailoverGroup | user (kubectl bloodraven ack-planned-failover-hold); the operator removes it | `<runID>`, the held run's status.plannedFailoverHold.runID. This key acknowledges an automation hold. An operator-minted run id cannot match another group, so the value needs no confirm= or uid= pair. The operator removes it after it clears the hold. | Public |
| `bloodraven.shipstream.io/rollout-admit` (annotation) | MysqlFailoverGroup | administrator | `true`. This key admits the group to the paced rollout of a release-driven pod change now, whatever the queue or a halt says. It is declarative: while it is set, every new release rolls this group without waiting for the slot. Remove it afterwards. | Public |
| `bloodraven.shipstream.io/rollout-release-slot` (annotation) | MysqlFailoverGroup | administrator | `true`. This key lets the paced rollout continue past this group: while it is set, the group's unfinished or stalled roll does not hold the rollout slot, so the next group is admitted. The group's own roll continues as before. | Public |
| `bloodraven.shipstream.io/reclone-site` (annotation) | MysqlFailoverGroup | user (kubectl bloodraven reclone); operator | `<site>:confirm=<metadata.name>:uid=<metadata.uid>`, plus `:gtidPrefix=<uuid prefix>` when the site has diverged. This key asks the operator to reclone one site from the current primary with CLONE INSTANCE, which wipes the site's datadir. When the site has a recorded divergent GTID set (status.sites[].divergentGtid), gtidPrefix= is required: at least 8 characters of the source UUID of the set's first entry. It proves the requester read the divergence. The operator also writes it to drain status.restoreReclones, and removes it when the clone is done or the request is rejected. | Public |
| `bloodraven.shipstream.io/revoke-deployment-leases` (annotation) | MysqlFailoverGroup | user; the operator removes it | any; its presence is the request. This key revokes every deployment lease the group holds. Lease admission stays closed while it is set; the operator removes it once every revocation has persisted, and a value changed meanwhile is a new request it handles first. | Public |
| `bloodraven.shipstream.io/rotate-keyring` (annotation) | MysqlFailoverGroup | user; the operator removes it | `<site>`. This key triggers an InnoDB master-key rotation on the named site. The operator refuses to rotate the active primary: rotate the replicas, run a planned failover, then rotate the former primary. | Public |
| `bloodraven.shipstream.io/release-pitr-archive-binding` (annotation) | MysqlFailoverGroup | user; the operator removes it | `<binding id>:confirm=<metadata.name>:uid=<metadata.uid>`. This key releases one PITR archive binding and deletes its key snapshots. The binding id is derived from the destination, so it recurs in a re-created group of the same name: the uid pair keeps a stale request from releasing the new group's binding. | Public |

## Failover record and planned-failover bookkeeping

| Key | On | Writer | Value and meaning | Stability |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `bloodraven.shipstream.io/last-failover`, `bloodraven.shipstream.io/last-failover-target` (annotation) | MysqlFailoverGroup | operator | an RFC 3339 UTC instant at second precision; the target site name. These keys copy the anti-flap record (status.lastFailover) to object metadata, so a status-write outage that overlaps an operator restart cannot lose the cooldown. Both are written in one patch on every promotion. | Operator-owned read-only |
| `bloodraven.shipstream.io/promotion-gtid-executed` (annotation) | MysqlFailoverGroup | operator | a GTID set. This key is the out-of-band copy of the promotion watermark (status.lastFailover.promotionGtidExecuted), written with `bloodraven.shipstream.io/last-failover` and `bloodraven.shipstream.io/last-failover-target`. Omitted above 64 KiB. Ignored unless `bloodraven.shipstream.io/promotion-gtid-executed-for` names the event the other two keys record. | Operator-owned read-only |
| `bloodraven.shipstream.io/promotion-gtid-executed-for` (annotation) | MysqlFailoverGroup | operator | `<last-failover> <last-failover-target>` (one space), for example `2026-11-04T10:00:00Z iad`. This key binds the watermark to its failover event, written and deleted in the same patch as `bloodraven.shipstream.io/promotion-gtid-executed`. A watermark whose binding does not name the event the other two keys record is no watermark. | Operator-owned read-only |
| `bloodraven.shipstream.io/clone-server-uuid` (annotation) | MysqlFailoverGroup | operator | `{"<site>":{"serverUUID":"<uuid>","previousCloneBegin":"<BEGIN_TIME>"}}`, where previousCloneBegin is BEGIN_TIME of the site's `performance_schema.clone_status` row before the clone (empty when it had none, omitted when it could not be read). This key records, before CLONE INSTANCE is issued into a site, the server_uuid the site had, so the check that every clone gives its recipient a new one (CloneServerUUIDNotRotated) is still made when the clone finishes after the operator that issued it restarted. A site's entry is removed once its clone has an outcome; the annotation is removed with the last entry. While an entry exists, the site's keyring stays unsealed under encryption at rest. | Internal (may change) |
| `bloodraven.shipstream.io/server-uuid-history` (annotation) | MysqlFailoverGroup | operator | `{"<site>":["<uuid>", "clone", "<uuid>", ...]}`, where `clone` stands for a clone issued into the site. This key records, per site and oldest first, the server_uuid values the operator has seen the site run under and where a clone into the site was issued (at most 8 entries per site). A site's replication receiver drops events that carry the site's own server_id, whatever server_uuid issued them, so a site whose volume came back from before a reclone lacks the transactions it issued under its later server_uuid and cannot get them by replication. The operator compares a returning site with the primary under every recorded server_uuid (status.sites[].lostGtid). When there is no primary and a promotion target is chosen, another site's set counts against a candidate only under the server_uuids recorded after the candidate's last clone and the one it runs under: what it lacks of an earlier one it gave up at that clone. The pre-clone server_uuid and the clone are written by the same write as the clone identity record, before the clone is issued. Removing the annotation narrows both checks to the site's current server_uuid until the operator has seen the others again. | Internal (may change) |
| `bloodraven.shipstream.io/planned-failover-status-fence` (annotation) | MysqlFailoverGroup | operator | an ISO 8601 basic UTC instant with nanoseconds, `20261104T100000.123456789Z`. This key is bumped with a write conditioned on the resourceVersion an ambiguous status write was made against. Its success proves that write can never commit. Each bump moves past the stored value. | Internal (may change) |
| `bloodraven.shipstream.io/planned-failover-terminal` (annotation) | MysqlFailoverGroup | operator | `{"schemaVersion":1,"runID":"<runID>","outcome":"<outcome>","reason":"<reason>","warnings":["<warning>"]}` (reason and warnings may be omitted). This key ends a run outside /status when its status writes stall. Every planned-failover predicate treats the run it names as terminal; a ManualRecoveryRequired marker is also a hold record. A marker with a schemaVersion the operator does not know is reported (Degraded=True/MetadataVersionUnsupported and a Warning Event) and proves no outcome, but one naming a run with outcome ManualRecoveryRequired still holds automation. | Internal (may change) |
| `bloodraven.shipstream.io/planned-failover-stall-since` (annotation) | MysqlFailoverGroup | operator | `<runID>:since=<YYYYMMDDThhmmssZ>`. This key is the durable start of the status-stall deadline. | Internal (may change) |
| `bloodraven.shipstream.io/planned-failover-manager-absent-since` (annotation) | MysqlFailoverGroup | operator | `<runID>:since=<YYYYMMDDThhmmssZ>`. This key is the durable start of the manager-absence deadline. | Internal (may change) |
| `bloodraven.shipstream.io/planned-failover-confirmed` (annotation) | MysqlFailoverGroup | operator | `<runID>:since=<YYYYMMDDThhmmssZ>`, the confirmation time. This key records, before the run releases its claim, that the run's promotion was confirmed, recorded and published, so a restart before the final status write does not take the released claim back. Removed when the run ends. | Internal (may change) |
| `bloodraven.shipstream.io/encryption-status-fence` (annotation) | MysqlFailoverGroup | operator | an RFC 3339 timestamp. This key is bumped to advance the group's resourceVersion, so a status write conditioned on an older version (one whose response was lost) can no longer commit. The write is what matters; nothing reads the value. | Internal (may change) |
| `bloodraven.shipstream.io/restore-confirm` (annotation) | the in-place restore Job | operator | the confirm token. This key is the spec.restoreInPlace.confirm token the in-place restore Job was created for, so a Job left over from an earlier request with the same name is not mistaken for the current one. | Internal (may change) |
| `bloodraven.shipstream.io/restore-backup-uid` (annotation) | restore Jobs (bootstrap and in-place) with a backupRef source | operator | the MysqlBackup's metadata.uid. This key records the MysqlBackup a restore Job was built from (source.backupRef). The Job is created only when that is the backup the restore holds (`restore-hold.bloodraven.shipstream.io/`). | Internal (may change) |

## Finalizers

Each finalizer is named after its kind. The operator adds and removes them; removing one by hand skips the cleanup it guards.

| Key | On | Writer | Value and meaning | Stability |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `bloodraven.shipstream.io/failover-group` (finalizer) | MysqlFailoverGroup | operator | none (a finalizer). This key runs the graceful-shutdown sequence (node taints removed, DNS records deleted) before a MysqlFailoverGroup is deleted. | Internal (may change) |
| `bloodraven.shipstream.io/mysqldatabase` (finalizer) | MysqlDatabase | operator | none (a finalizer). This key guards the MySQL-side cleanup of a MysqlDatabase. | Internal (may change) |
| `bloodraven.shipstream.io/mysqlbackup` (finalizer) | MysqlBackup | operator | none (a finalizer). This key guards the artifact cleanup of a MysqlBackup. | Internal (may change) |
| `bloodraven.shipstream.io/mysqlbackup-verification` (finalizer) | MysqlBackupVerification | operator | none (a finalizer). This key guards the cleanup of a MysqlBackupVerification's resources. | Internal (may change) |

## Group routing labels

The operator puts these on the objects it manages for a MysqlFailoverGroup (pods, Services, Deployments, StatefulSets, Secrets). Services, NetworkPolicies and monitors select on them. Operator labels win over spec.podLabels.

| Key | On | Writer | Value and meaning | Stability |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `bloodraven.shipstream.io/failover-group` (label) | managed objects and pods; MysqlBackup, MysqlBackupVerification | operator; kubectl bloodraven backup and verify; user, on a MysqlBackup or MysqlBackupVerification it creates | the group name. This key names the owning MysqlFailoverGroup. It is also on MysqlBackups and MysqlBackupVerifications (spec.failoverGroupRef), and kubectl bloodraven sets it on the ones it creates. The one place a user writes it is a MysqlBackup or MysqlBackupVerification created by hand: set it to spec.failoverGroupRef, with `bloodraven.shipstream.io/backup-profile`. On every object the operator manages it is the operator's. | Operator-owned read-only |
| `bloodraven.shipstream.io/site` (label) | managed objects and pods | operator | the site name. This key names the site. It is part of every Deployment and StatefulSet selector, which is immutable: a workload whose selector differs from the one the operator renders is refused (Degraded=True/WorkloadSelectorMismatch). | Operator-owned read-only |
| `bloodraven.shipstream.io/role` (label) | MySQL pods | operator | `primary` or `replica`. This key is the site's role, set on the live pods each health poll. The primary and replica Services select on it. | Operator-owned read-only |
| `bloodraven.shipstream.io/healthy` (label) | MySQL pods | operator | `true` or `false`. This key is the site's verdict from its last health poll. The replica Service and a ReadOnly site's Service select on "true". | Operator-owned read-only |
| `bloodraven.shipstream.io/dragonfly-role` (label) | Dragonfly pods | operator | `master` or `replica`. This key is a Dragonfly pod's operator-assigned role. The active Service selects on it together with `bloodraven.shipstream.io/dragonfly-traffic`. | Operator-owned read-only |
| `bloodraven.shipstream.io/dragonfly-traffic` (label) | Dragonfly pods | operator | `true`, or absent. This key gates whether a Dragonfly pod is eligible for the active Service, which selects "true". A planned failover removes it from the source pod before the takeover, so the Service sheds the old endpoint first. | Operator-owned read-only |

| `bloodraven.shipstream.io/keyring-version` (label) | keyring escrow Secrets | operator; the keyring escrow recovery runbook reads it | an integer. This key is the escrow version on a site's keyring escrow Secret. | Internal (may change) |
| `bloodraven.shipstream.io/keyring-digest` (annotation) | keyring escrow Secrets | operator | `sha256:<hex>`. This key records the digest of the escrowed keyring bytes. It is informational: the operator always recomputes it. | Internal (may change) |
| `bloodraven.shipstream.io/spec-hash` (annotation) | site Deployments and other managed objects | operator | a hash. This key is the hash of the rendered spec of a managed object; a difference starts an ordered update. | Internal (may change) |

This key names the operator release (its renderer identity) that last wrote the workload's pod template. A workload that carries another value, or none, and whose template the running operator would change is rolled only once the group is admitted to the paced rollout (status.rollout). | Internal (may change) |
| `bloodraven.shipstream.io/managed-service-annotations` (annotation) | Services | operator | a JSON list of annotation keys. This key lists the Service annotations the operator manages, so it can remove one that leaves the spec. | Internal (may change) |
| `bloodraven.shipstream.io/credential-hash` (annotation) | credential Secrets | operator | a hash. This key records the hash of the credentials last applied. | Internal (may change) |
| `bloodraven.shipstream.io/system-schema-restriction` (annotation) | credential Secrets | operator | a hash. This key records the credential hash for which the application user's system-schema restriction last succeeded. | Internal (may change) |
| `bloodraven.shipstream.io/dragonfly-load-hold` (annotation) | Dragonfly pods | operator | an RFC 3339 time, when the hold started. This key marks a Dragonfly pod whose traffic the operator holds off until it has loaded its snapshot: the active site of a snapshot-restore upgrade that ended while it was still loading. While it is set, the operator removes the pod's `bloodraven.shipstream.io/dragonfly-traffic` again whoever restored it, and it removes the annotation once the site answers as loaded. | Internal (may change) |

## Holds

A hold keeps an object that a running operation reads. Holds form one family, `<kind>-hold.bloodraven.shipstream.io/<id>`, so every hold of a kind is found by one prefix match. Removing a hold by hand while its holder runs can delete data under it.

| Key | On | Writer | Value and meaning | Stability |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `verification-hold.bloodraven.shipstream.io/<verification uid>` (annotation) | MysqlBackup; PITR archive key snapshot Secrets | operator | the verification's name. This key marks a MysqlBackup, and a PITR archive key snapshot, that a MysqlBackupVerification is reading. The full key is the prefix followed by the verification's uid. Retention, the artifact-cleanup finalizer and the PITR binlog cutoff leave the object alone while a hold on it is live, also while the verification is Terminating. | Operator-owned read-only |
| `restore-hold.bloodraven.shipstream.io/<hold ID>` (annotation) | MysqlBackup | operator | the restoring group's name. This key marks a MysqlBackup that a restore (spec.initFromBackup or spec.restoreInPlace with source.backupRef) of a MysqlFailoverGroup in the same namespace is reading. The full key is the prefix followed by the hold ID the restore recorded in status.restore.backupRef.holdID or status.restoreInPlace.backupRef.holdID. Retention, the artifact-cleanup finalizer and the PITR binlog cutoff leave the backup alone while the hold is live: until the restore is Succeeded or Failed and its Job's pods have stopped. | Operator-owned read-only |

## Node taint

| Key | On | Writer | Value and meaning | Stability |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `<namespace>.db-readonly.bloodraven.shipstream.io/<group>` (taint) | Node | operator; users tolerate it | `true`, effect `NoExecute`. The operator puts this taint, with effect NoExecute, on a site's nodes (spec.sites[].taintNodeSelector) while the site is read only, so pods that do not tolerate it are evicted; workloads that must keep running there tolerate it. The namespace is part of the key, so two groups of the same name in different namespaces never share a taint. The prefix is at most 100 characters (a 63-character namespace) and the name part is the group name. | Public |
